difficultyReason: Two-sentence argument with an explicit conclusion marker ("therefore"). The target claim sits before the marker and plainly provides the evidence, so only the supporting-premise answer fits.
stimulus: Regular aerobic exercise has been shown in numerous clinical studies to lower resting blood pressure in adults with mild hypertension. Therefore, physicians treating patients with mild hypertension should routinely recommend aerobic exercise as part of the treatment plan.
questionStem: The claim that regular aerobic exercise has been shown in numerous clinical studies to lower resting blood pressure in adults with mild hypertension plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the main conclusion of the argument.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a premise offered in support of the argument's main conclusion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a claim the argument is designed to discredit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a generalization that the argument's conclusion is meant to explain.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is background information unrelated to the argument's reasoning.

explanations.correct: The explicit marker "therefore" introduces the recommendation to physicians as the conclusion. The claim about clinical studies is the evidence given for that recommendation, i.e., a supporting premise.
explanations.A: The main conclusion is the recommendation about physicians' practice, not the claim about clinical studies.
explanations.C: Nothing in the argument signals disagreement with the cited studies; they are endorsed, not discredited.
explanations.D: The argument uses the studies to support, not to explain away, the recommendation.
explanations.E: The claim is load-bearing evidence, not extraneous context.

difficultyReason: The conclusion marker "thus" introduces the target claim, which follows a single supporting observation. Textual position uniquely fixes the answer as main conclusion.
stimulus: Every time the library has extended its weekend hours in the past, student check-outs of print books have risen by more than 20 percent within a month. Thus, if the library extends its weekend hours next semester, student check-outs of print books will very likely rise by a similar margin.
questionStem: The claim that if the library extends its weekend hours next semester, student check-outs of print books will very likely rise by a similar margin plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a premise offered in support of the main conclusion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is an assumption on which the argument's premise depends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the main conclusion of the argument.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a counterexample meant to undermine a general claim.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a prediction cited only to be rejected.

explanations.correct: The word "thus" introduces the target claim as the point the prior sentence is offered to support. That makes the target claim the main conclusion.
explanations.A: The supporting premise is the historical pattern in the first sentence, not the target claim.
explanations.B: The claim is explicitly stated, not left unstated as an assumption.
explanations.D: The argument treats the target as what follows from the evidence, not as a counterexample.
explanations.E: The author endorses, rather than rejects, the prediction.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence argument with "so" signaling the conclusion. The target claim sits in the premise position and is the sole reason offered.
stimulus: Critic: Most successful technology startups in the region have relied on at least one senior engineer with more than ten years of industry experience. So Beldon Software, a new regional startup currently without any senior engineer, is unlikely to succeed unless it hires one.
questionStem: The claim that most successful technology startups in the region have relied on at least one senior engineer with more than ten years of industry experience plays which one of the following roles in the critic's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the main conclusion of the critic's argument.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a subsidiary conclusion drawn from the claim about Beldon Software.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a premise offered to support the critic's main conclusion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a claim the critic acknowledges but rejects.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a counterexample to an earlier generalization.

explanations.correct: The critic's point — signaled by "so" — is about Beldon Software's prospects. The generalization about regional startups is the evidence offered for that point, i.e., a supporting premise.
explanations.A: The main conclusion is the prediction about Beldon Software, not the generalization.
explanations.B: The generalization supports, rather than is supported by, the Beldon-specific claim.
explanations.D: The critic endorses the generalization; nothing signals disagreement.
explanations.E: No earlier generalization is offered for the claim to counter.

difficultyReason: Clear two-sentence argument with "hence" marking the conclusion. Target claim is the conclusion; only one choice matches the textual position.
stimulus: The fine for overdue municipal parking meters has not been raised in more than twenty years, and during that time the average cost of city services funded by such fines has more than doubled. Hence, the city council should increase the overdue-meter fine at its next session.
questionStem: The claim that the city council should increase the overdue-meter fine at its next session plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a premise offered in support of the argument's main conclusion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is the main conclusion of the argument.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a claim the argument treats as already widely accepted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a counterproposal the argument ultimately rejects.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a factual observation about current council practice.

explanations.correct: "Hence" introduces the recommendation as the point the prior observations are offered to support. That makes the recommendation the main conclusion.
explanations.A: The supporting premises are the stagnant fine and the rising costs; the recommendation is what they support.
explanations.C: The argument is arguing for the recommendation, not assuming it is already accepted.
explanations.D: The argument endorses the recommendation, not rejects it.
explanations.E: The recommendation is prescriptive, not a description of current practice.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence argument with "therefore" marking the conclusion. Target sits in premise position and is the only evidence cited.
stimulus: Linguist: Children exposed to a second language before age five consistently achieve native-like pronunciation in that language, while those who first encounter it after age twelve almost never do. Therefore, the window for acquiring native-like pronunciation in a second language closes well before adolescence.
questionStem: The claim that children exposed to a second language before age five consistently achieve native-like pronunciation in that language, while those who first encounter it after age twelve almost never do plays which one of the following roles in the linguist's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the linguist's main conclusion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is the empirical finding offered in support of the linguist's main conclusion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is an alternative view the linguist is arguing against.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a subsidiary conclusion supported by the claim about the pronunciation window.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is an assumption the linguist leaves unstated.

explanations.correct: The linguist concludes, after "therefore," that the acquisition window closes before adolescence. The target claim reports the observations that drive that conclusion — a supporting premise.
explanations.A: The main conclusion is the claim about when the pronunciation window closes.
explanations.C: The linguist endorses the empirical finding; it is not treated as an opposing view.
explanations.D: The target supports, rather than is supported by, the window claim.
explanations.E: The claim is explicitly stated, so it is not an unstated assumption.

difficultyReason: Short two-sentence argument with an explicit "therefore" conclusion marker. The target claim is clearly the main conclusion.
stimulus: In the three counties where a deposit was placed on beverage containers, roadside litter dropped by more than 60 percent within two years, while in neighboring counties without a deposit, roadside litter remained essentially unchanged. Therefore, container-deposit programs are an effective means of reducing roadside litter.
questionStem: The claim that container-deposit programs are an effective means of reducing roadside litter plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a background observation used to introduce the topic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a premise offered in support of the argument's main conclusion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the main conclusion of the argument.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a hypothesis the argument is designed to refute.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a prediction that the argument does not actually defend.

explanations.correct: The word "therefore" introduces the general claim about container-deposit programs as the point the comparison between counties is offered to support. That general claim is the main conclusion.
explanations.A: Background would precede the evidence, not follow "therefore."
explanations.B: The supporting premise is the comparison among counties; the general claim is what it supports.
explanations.D: The argument endorses, rather than refutes, the general claim.
explanations.E: The argument explicitly offers the county comparison as support for the claim.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence ethics argument with explicit "thus" marker. The target claim is the premise and is the sole reason cited for the conclusion.
stimulus: Ethicist: A person who makes a promise is obligated to keep it unless doing so would cause significant harm to others. Thus, Dr. Karimi, who promised to speak at the conference, should honor that promise, since her speaking would not cause such harm.
questionStem: The claim that a person who makes a promise is obligated to keep it unless doing so would cause significant harm to others plays which one of the following roles in the ethicist's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the main conclusion of the ethicist's argument.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a general principle offered in support of the main conclusion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is an exception to the main conclusion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a moral view the ethicist is arguing against.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is an observation about Dr. Karimi's specific situation.

explanations.correct: The ethicist's conclusion, signaled by "thus," concerns Dr. Karimi. The general principle about promises is the reason offered for that conclusion — a supporting premise in the form of a principle.
explanations.A: The main conclusion is about Dr. Karimi specifically, not the general principle.
explanations.C: The principle frames the conclusion; it is not carved out as an exception.
explanations.D: The ethicist endorses the principle rather than arguing against it.
explanations.E: The principle is general, not a fact about Dr. Karimi's situation.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence environmental argument; "therefore" clearly marks the conclusion, which is the target claim.
stimulus: The coastal wetlands at Marsh Point serve as the primary breeding ground for three species of shorebirds whose populations have declined sharply elsewhere in the region. Therefore, protecting Marsh Point from further development should be a priority for the state wildlife agency.
questionStem: The claim that protecting Marsh Point from further development should be a priority for the state wildlife agency plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is an observation about the region's shorebirds.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a premise offered in support of a broader claim about wildlife policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the main conclusion of the argument.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a policy the argument is designed to discredit.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a claim that the argument takes to be already established.

explanations.correct: The recommendation follows "therefore" and is what the earlier ecological observation is offered to support. That makes it the main conclusion.
explanations.A: It is a prescriptive policy claim, not an observation about shorebirds.
explanations.B: The argument ends with this recommendation; no broader claim is drawn from it.
explanations.D: The argument endorses, rather than discredits, the recommendation.
explanations.E: The argument is arguing for the recommendation; it is not treated as already settled.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence history argument with explicit conclusion marker "so." The target claim is a supporting premise and the only evidence offered.
stimulus: Historian: Every major city in the empire that survived the plague of 432 had a fortified harbor, while nearly every city without a fortified harbor was abandoned within a decade. So fortified harbors were a key factor in whether a city survived the plague years.
questionStem: The claim that every major city in the empire that survived the plague of 432 had a fortified harbor, while nearly every city without a fortified harbor was abandoned within a decade plays which one of the following roles in the historian's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the historian's main conclusion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a claim offered as evidence for the historian's main conclusion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is an opposing view the historian is arguing against.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a sub-conclusion derived from a claim about fortified harbors.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is background information unrelated to the argument's reasoning.

explanations.correct: The historian concludes, after "so," that fortified harbors were a key factor in survival. The pattern reported before "so" is the evidence — a supporting premise.
explanations.A: The main conclusion is the causal claim about fortified harbors.
explanations.C: The historian endorses, rather than opposes, the reported pattern.
explanations.D: The pattern supports the causal claim, not the other way around.
explanations.E: The pattern is the central evidence, not extraneous background.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence arts argument with explicit "therefore" conclusion marker. Target claim is the main conclusion; textual position uniquely determines the answer.
stimulus: Museums that reduce admission fees on weekday evenings in cities comparable to ours have reported sustained increases in overall attendance and in revenue from gift-shop sales. Therefore, the Westlake Museum should introduce reduced weekday-evening admission fees.
questionStem: The claim that the Westlake Museum should introduce reduced weekday-evening admission fees plays which one of the following roles in the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a premise offered in support of the main conclusion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a claim the argument takes to be already widely accepted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a description of what other museums have reported.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the main conclusion of the argument.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a prediction that the argument goes on to reject.

explanations.correct: "Therefore" introduces the recommendation about the Westlake Museum as the point the first sentence is offered to support. That recommendation is the main conclusion.
explanations.A: The supporting premise is the report about comparable museums; the recommendation is what it supports.
explanations.B: The argument is arguing for the recommendation, not treating it as already accepted.
explanations.C: The description of other museums is in the first sentence; the target is about the Westlake Museum specifically.
explanations.E: The argument endorses the recommendation rather than rejecting it.
